value: Within the control group, high-calorie food images were generally effective in activating cortical regions of interest relative to control images, with subcortical activation only in the hippocampus.
Within the obese group, high-calorie food images elicited significant activation in all regions of interest except the hypothalamus.

Compared with controls, obese women showed greater activation to high-calorie food pictures in a wide range of brain regions thought to mediate motivational and emotional responses to foods and food cues.

value: Within the control group, low-calorie food images were generally effective in activating cortical regions of interest relative to control images.
Within the obese group, low-calorie food images activated the same regions as high-calorie foods except for medial orbitofrontal cortex, ventral tegmental area, and ventral pallidum.

In the between-group comparison, results for low-calorie foods were mixed: obese participants showed greater activation than controls in the caudate and putamen, whereas controls showed greater activation in the anterior cingulate cortex, medial prefrontal cortex, and lateral orbitofrontal cortex.

The rationale for testing the differences between the activation in response to the high-calorie foods minus the low-calorie foods is that this comparison should most clearly reflect the response to relative reward value

value: For the high-calorie versus low-calorie contrast, high-calorie foods produced more activation than low-calorie foods in six regions of interest in the obese group, and no region showed greater activation to low-calorie foods.

In the control group, high-calorie foods produced greater activation only in the dorsal caudate, whereas low-calorie foods produced greater activation in the lateral orbitofrontal cortex, medial prefrontal cortex, and anterior cingulate cortex.

The high-calorie versus low-calorie difference was significantly greater in obese participants than controls in ten regions of interest, while controls showed greater activation in the right dorsal caudate and right lateral orbitofrontal cortex for the reverse comparison.
